items: Appetite
Wants something now. Loud, honest about what it wants, and rarely your interest.
Approval
Wants you to be thought well of. Quiet, respectable, and it eats most lives.
Interest
Asks what you will be glad you built in five years. The only voice on your side.
The automatic yes
He does the revision that night. The portfolio stays closed and resentment collects the cost.
The flat refusal
His evening is protected, but he never asked whether this client matters to his future.
The renegotiated scope
“Billed at my day rate, and you’ll have it Monday.” He keeps the client and spends Thursday on the portfolio.
The tantrum
Doing whatever you feel like and calling it self-care. Appetite with a philosophy attached.
The martyr
Giving everything away, then resenting everyone who took it. Approval in charge.
The secret plan
Deciding what matters, protecting nothing and telling nobody. A plan with no cost and no witness is a daydream.

W01-L01:8.sub: Three voices compete for every hour you have. Only one of them is yours.

W01-L01:14.sub: Winning the argument can cost you the thing you are building.

W01-L01:20.sub: Where did appetite write a line? Is there a real cost? Fix at least one line.

items: The automatic yes
He packs boxes all evening. His doctrine lasted one day.
The defensive biography
Four paragraphs of reasons. Now his friend has a list to argue with, and both feel guilty.
The clean no
“Can’t tonight, I’m working on something I’ve committed to. I can give you three hours on Saturday.”
A fast yes is a habit. Slow it down until it becomes a decision.
You owe people an answer. You do not owe them a defence.
Warm and clear beats long and guilty, every time.
A verdict
Says what you are. It can never be tested, so it never changes.
An experiment
Asks what happens when you do one small thing.
Evidence
Arrives by the end of the week. You only need to be curious enough to check.
What am I agreeing to?
Include the preparation, the travel, the waiting and the follow-up.
Where does it come from?
Name the actual hours, the energy or the money.
Is it worth more?
Compare it with the best thing it replaces. Sometimes the answer is yes.

W02-L02:7.title: Decide. Influence. Respond.
W02-L02:7.sub: Influence is partial. Do not pretend you control everything, and do not collapse into thinking you control nothing.

items: Nobody can open it
A broken link, the wrong permissions, a file that only works on your laptop.
Nobody asked for it
Built for an audience that turned out not to exist, or wanted something slightly different.
Nobody finished it
Ninety per cent of four things and one hundred per cent of none.
Frequent
You do it at least weekly, so the saving adds up quickly.
Structured
The shape is the same each time and only the details change.
Checkable
You can tell in a minute or two whether the output is right.
Low stakes
A mistake costs you minutes, not a client. Start there.
Trust it completely
Fast, right up until the week it invents a figure and a client spots it.
Never build it
Ten hours a week by hand, for as long as she does this work. Safe, and slowly expensive.
Draft, then verify
A ten-minute draft, every figure checked against her data. Forty minutes instead of two hours.

W04-L01:9.title: Know. Infer. Ask.
W04-L01:9.sub: An inferred motive is not a fact. Write the guess down and label it honestly, then ask.

items: Reward
What gets this person praised, paid or promoted?
Fear
What would get them blamed if it went wrong? Fear often explains more than reward does.
Measure
Which number is their boss actually looking at?
First order
The result today. They say yes, and you get the deal.
Second order
What that result changes. They now expect the same terms next time.
Third order
What that change sets up. Other clients hear about it, and your prices quietly drop.
Yes
He wins the sale, anchors his price low for years and delivers weaker videos.
Never
He protects his price and offers nothing else. The client walks.
Trade
“I can’t move the rate for this scope. I can do four videos, or one paid pilot at full rate.”
Cave
She accepts because she is tired. The first faulty batch could end the project.
Win
She calls it a disgrace. It feels good for ten seconds and burns a bridge in a small industry.
Leave, with an alternative
“These terms don’t work for me. Come back to the original minimum and I’ll sign this week.”
No margin
He spends his slot refreshing the page and apologising. He shows nothing.
Margin for everything
Five backup plans, and the main feature never finished.
Proportionate margin
He opens the local copy and shows the core in five minutes, calm because he had already decided.
